todo_line: - [ ] 004 Implement and test explicit custom-group-removal follow cleanup through public Messaging APIs, including manual and auto-follow sources, idempotent stale-safe remove/re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behaviour.
outcome: Complete task 004 with causal membership-generation ordering and durable use-case completion so every pre-removal manual or auto-follow is cleared, while first-delivered or replayed old cleanup can never erase a follow established after a genuine re-add.
scope: Revise the current task-004 candidate in place. Retain its existing public `Memba.Membership.Policies.ClearRemovedGroupMemberFollows` to `Memba.Messaging` collaboration, projection-lag barrier, effective-access-union check, and authoritative unfollow fact; do not create a second cleanup process.

Replace per-conversation cleanup-ID-only ordering with a durable generation/version contract derived from the Club-owned custom-group membership history. Messaging must distinguish a pre-removal follow from a genuinely newer post-re-add follow even when the old removal reaches that conversation for the first time.

Carry the causal membership generation through public Messaging commands/facts for all follow-establishing sources used by this obligation: explicit manual follow, root-sender auto-follow, and reply-author auto-follow. Ensure the root `ConversationFollowers` write model can authoritatively order reply-only auto-follow state rather than relying only on the follow projection.

Define replay-compatible semantics for historic `GroupMemberAdded`, `GroupMemberRemoved`, `MessageSent`, `ConversationFollowed`, and `ConversationUnfollowed` facts whose new ordering fields are absent. Preserve old event readability and the existing Club aggregate decision/event vocabulary.

Make cleanup safe on first delayed delivery and historical replay for conversations created after the removal, conversations previously cleaned before cleanup tokens existed, and conversations originally skipped because another active group supplied access. A cleanup older than the current follow must be a no-op; cleanup at or after the followed generation must clear it; delayed stale follow work must not resurrect state past a recorded cleanup cutoff.

Close the controlled remove/re-add/follow race: if `GroupMemberAdded` has committed and another process establishes a valid new follow while old cleanup is delayed, the old removal must not erase that newer follow, and pre-removal follows must not silently resume.

Make successful custom-group add/remove application-service calls await the cleanup handler through a durable EventStore checkpoint independently of whether the dispatch emitted an event. Preserve `:ok` and caller-selected Commanded return modes, make `consistency: :eventual` honor the documented completion promise, and make an event-free exact removal retry wait for the original pending cleanup.
Normalize both `:ok` and `{:ok, result}` from per-conversation public Messaging unfollow dispatches as successful cleanup outcomes; propagate typed errors without a case-clause crash.

Keep unrelated-conversation follows and shared-conversation follows with surviving effective access intact. Keep Everyone and Admin removal facts as direct cleanup no-ops, and add explicit proof for both system groups.

Correct and extend focused aggregate/integration tests to prove generation ordering, first delayed delivery, historical/legacy replay, later-created and shared-access-skipped conversations, completion for `:eventual` and exact retries, all return modes, all follow sources, projection lag, and system-group no-ops.
scope_exclusions: Do not change task 001's accepted custom-group removal authorization, actor/target validation, self/last-member behavior, role preservation, system-group rejection, or `GroupMemberRemoved`-only transition semantics except for backward-compatible generation/version data required by task 004.
Do not implement the broader group/conversation query and action authorization, provider-handoff reauthorization, queued-delivery cancellation, or open-LiveView refresh assigned to tasks 009-011.
Do not add Leave/Remove controls, confirmation dialogs, member-row changes, former-member surfaces, or empty-group UI behavior assigned to tasks 012-014.
Do not edit iteration-064 acceptance feature files or implement the browser/domain acceptance layer assigned to tasks 015-016.
Do not write Membership state directly from Messaging or Messaging projections directly from Membership; keep cross-context effects behind the existing public APIs and event-sourced commands/facts.
Do not redesign unrelated delivery, multi-group conversation editing, projection infrastructure, or the Club membership/role lifecycle.
Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, browser acceptance, or another unscoped full-suite command; task 017 and the deterministic `dev_check` node own the final repository gate.

references.facts: Implementation Plan 2 and the acceptance/open-technical-decision text require public Messaging APIs, idempotent facts, manual and root/reply auto-follow cleanup, stale remove/re-add safety, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behavior.

Iteration 062 established the origin-replaying Membership-to-Messaging cleanup boundary and requires departure/rejoin ordering; iteration 064 extends that same collaboration to explicit custom-group removal.
Membership owns group membership and Messaging owns follow state. Cross-context coordination must use public context APIs, not another context's aggregates or projection storage.

The Club stream is the authoritative membership lifecycle and identity boundary. Derive causal group-membership generation/version data from this history while preserving historic events and system-group policy consequences.

`add_custom_group_member/2` and `remove_custom_group_member/2` currently add the cleanup handler only through dispatch consistency. `include_removed_group_member_follows_consistency/1` leaves `:eventual` unchanged, and an exact event-free retry gives Commanded no new event to wait on.
The Club aggregate serializes `GroupMemberAdded`/`GroupMemberRemoved`; an exact inactive-member removal returns no events, while a re-add is authoritative as soon as its event appends.

The strong origin-replaying handler currently derives a cleanup ID from the removal event and delegates to public Messaging cleanup. Preserve this boundary, but supply sufficient causal generation/version information for first-delivery safety.

`clear_removed_group_member_follows/2` waits for Message/access/follow projections, discovers conversations by removed group, preserves surviving authoritative access, and dispatches public unfollows. Its reducer currently accepts only `:ok`, although returning modes can produce `{:ok, result}`.

The current candidate stores completed cleanup IDs only after a `ConversationUnfollowed` is emitted. It therefore cannot order first delivery of an old removal against a newer follow, and the root aggregate still cannot see reply-only `MessageSent` auto-follow state.

The projection combines manual follow/unfollow and both root and reply `MessageSent` auto-follow facts. The revised write-side contract must retain deterministic projection behavior without making projection rows the authority.

The current replay test first records the new cleanup token before re-add/follow and therefore proves duplicate-token handling only. Add controlled first-delivery, historical/legacy, later-conversation, shared-skip, suspended-handler race, completion-mode, exact-retry, and direct Admin no-op cases.

Current aggregate coverage proves cleanup-token idempotency after the token exists. Extend it with older/newer follow-vs-cleanup generations, delayed stale follow work, already-following generation refresh, and absent-field replay semantics.
Existing focused coverage establishes root and reply `MessageSent` auto-follow projection behavior; retain it while introducing authoritative generation ordering.
Existing tests establish effective access composed across group grants; cleanup must preserve a global conversation/person follow while another active group still supplies access.
The current lag regression expects cleanup to wait for access projection visibility. Preserve that behavior while making ordering safe across delayed and replayed removal work.
Use focused tests, `start_supervised!/1`, monitors, `Task.yield/2`, handler suspension, or deterministic synchronization primitives rather than sleeps for race coverage.

constraints: Keep task identity 004 and revise the existing candidate; do not reset the bounded revision visit by inventing another task for the same rejected work.

Use the accepted actor-bearing custom-group add/remove paths and existing `GroupMemberAdded`/`GroupMemberRemoved` facts. Any added event fields must be backward compatible with stored facts and preserve task-001 event meaning.
Use Club-owned membership history as the causal source and Messaging-owned facts as the follow authority. Do not directly mutate another bounded context's projection or query its aggregate internals.
Per-removal cleanup ID deduplication may remain as a retry aid, but it is not sufficient ordering. Prove first delivery of stale work cannot erase a newer post-re-add follow.

The follow is conversation/person scoped rather than group scoped. Preserve it whenever another active group still grants effective read access, and ensure a previously skipped old cleanup cannot later invalidate a newer follow.
Cover true manual follow, root-sender auto-follow, and reply-author auto-follow. Projection-only false state is not sufficient evidence that write-side cleanup is authoritative.

Successful public add/remove return values and caller-selected Commanded modes must remain intact while the documented cleanup completion contract holds for default, `:strong`, `:eventual`, list-based consistency, and event-free exact retries.
Preserve `ClearRemovedGroupMemberFollows` origin replay and independent projection rebuilds. Ordinary projector reset/replay must not itself dispatch external cleanup side effects.
Keep new fields and aggregate replay tolerant of historic facts lacking generation/version data; add direct legacy-shape tests.
Limit edits to the membership-generation, cleanup/follow ordering, completion orchestration, and focused test seam. Leave tasks 009-017 untouched.
completion_evidence_required: List changed paths and describe the selected causal membership generation/version and durable completion mechanisms, including historical absent-field semantics.
Report exit statuses and test counts for both focused test commands on the exact handoff state, plus `git diff --check`.

Identify tests where an old removal reaches a conversation for the first time after genuine re-add/follow and where the conversation was created later, previously legacy-cleaned, or previously skipped for shared access; show the newer follow survives.
Show a deterministically controlled suspended-handler remove/re-add/follow race in which pre-removal follows do not resume and a valid newer follow is not erased.

Identify write-side facts/tests proving authoritative cleanup and generation ordering for manual follow, root auto-follow, and reply-only auto-follow, including delayed stale follow work and replay/idempotency.

Show default and `consistency: :eventual` add/remove completion, an event-free exact retry after the original cleanup is delayed or timed out, preservation of caller-selected return modes, and successful `{:ok, result}` cleanup handling.
Show unrelated and shared-access follows remain intact, access-projection lag cannot falsely acknowledge cleanup, and direct Everyone and Admin removal facts both remain no-ops.

Confirm accepted task-001 behavior remains unchanged: explicit removal emits only the reusable Membership removal fact for a transition, exact retry emits no new fact, and club membership/roles plus system-group guards are preserved.

latest_review.summary: Per-conversation cleanup IDs are insufficient because first delayed or historical cleanup can erase a newer follow for later-created, legacy-cleaned, or shared-access-skipped conversations. Close the remove/re-add/follow race with generation/version ordering; make `:eventual` and event-free exact retries await durable cleanup; accept `{:ok, result}` cleanup returns; and add direct Admin system-group no-op coverage.

latest_worker_result.summary: The candidate introduced cleanup IDs, projection barriers, authoritative access preservation, and focused tests with reported 32- and 36-test passing suites, but those tests do not cover the review's first-delivery generation, controlled re-add race, event-free retry, return-mode, or Admin no-op gaps.
